title: Microsoft Purview: unified Classifiers page for sensitive information types and trainable classifiers
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, permissions and commands are supported, and all five Learn links opened successfully. The licensing field understates published product-level licensing, and the role-group path omits headings; both are minor corrections.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence specific to the new Classifiers experience is published.
claims.quote: The per-user licensing model is the familiar Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 model. It remains unchanged. This licensing model enables you to apply Microsoft Purview controls and protections to Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint-based assets.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the opening licensing paragraph and notes with: 'The Classifiers management experience uses the existing Purview entitlement. Microsoft documents the Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 per-user licensing model for Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint assets; users assigned a Purview role for portal use require the appropriate licence. A licence specific to the new Classifiers page is not yet published. Credential scanning SITs require an E5 licence.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-billing-models and https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description. In Open questions and the cost rationale, narrow 'Licensing is Not yet published' to 'Licensing specific to the new page is Not yet published'.
